params.body:
## Why

A dealer fetches a chassis number, sees the sheet fill up, prints the showroom poster and gets
"Energy Card not available". The NOx value the supplier returned never arrived anywhere, and the
dealer typed it over from the certificate by hand - which is why so many Energy Cards could not be
made. This is finding X-44 / open point O-10, rule R S1-7.6.

## Where it went wrong

`OwnStockService::createAutoConnectLookupMapping()` maps the AutoConnect response block by block.
`BlockE` carries the emissions. Two lines write columns on the vehicle (`nedc_emission`,
`wltp_emission`); NOx wrote to an option instead:

```php
$noxemmission = $optionRepo->first(['name_nl' => 'NOX-uitstoot', 'active' => 1]);
...
if (filled(optional($block)->NoxEngineTest) && !is_null($noxemmission)) {
    $afterUpdate['option'][$noxemmission->id] = optional($block)->NoxEngineTest;
}
```

**That option does not exist.** A query on staging, which runs a copy of the production data,
returns nothing for `Option::where('name_nl','like','%nox%')`. So `first(...)` returned null, the
`!is_null($noxemmission)` guard never fired, and the fetched value was dropped without a log line,
without an error, without a trace. Not "written to the wrong place": written nowhere.

Meanwhile `vehicles.nox_value` stayed null. That column is what `AfficheController::check()` counts
(`nox_value <= 0 or null`, the warning before printing) and what `AfficheController::index()` prints
on the card. Hence the "NOX, punt 48 op het COC" field on the sheet that always had to be filled in
by hand.

## What changed

The dead option path is gone (both the lookup and the write), and the value goes to the column, in
the style of the two lines above it:

```php
if (filled(optional($block)->NoxEngineTest)) {
    $nox_value = Custom::parseAmount(optional($block)->NoxEngineTest);
    if (!is_null($nox_value)) {
        $vehicle['nox_value'] = $nox_value;
    }
}
```

`vehicles.nox_value` is `double(15,2)` while the block may carry "22 mg/km" or a comma decimal
"0,4". `Custom::parseAmount` is the parser this codebase already uses for exactly that (it exists
because of finding X-08, the price that came back as 15,00) and it returns null rather than
throwing. A value it cannot read is left out of the array, so the column keeps whatever it had.
Nothing throws on a malformed value, and no lookup can fail because of this line.

## The option: removed, not kept

The brief's safe default was to keep filling the option as well. That default does not apply: there
is nothing to preserve. Grepped before deciding, and each check points the same way:

- Nothing in the repo reads the NOx option. The only two name-based references to "NOX-uitstoot"
  anywhere were the two lines in `OwnStockService` that this PR removes.
- `XML.php` exports `$vehicle->filledInOptions` generically, so *if* the option existed it would
  reach the Modix / Hexon feed. It does not exist, so nothing was ever exported from it and nothing
  disappears from the feed now.
- No PDF template and no website page mentions it.
- Confirmed against data by Shane's query on staging: no option row whose name contains "nox".

So keeping the write would be keeping a line that writes to a null id behind a guard that never
passes - dead code that made the bug look handled for years.

**One thing to check separately:** the neighbouring line for `FuelConsumptionCombined` does the same
`first(['name_nl' => 'Verbruik gecombineerd', 'active' => 1])`. I left it alone, as asked, and I
cannot query production from here. What the code says: unlike the NOx option, that one **does** have
a reader - `AfficheController::energycard()` line 370 looks the option up by the same name to print
the consumption on the card, and rule R S2-9.5 records that a missing one prints "??". So either the
option exists and both ends work, or it is equally dead and every Energy Card has been printing "??"
for consumption. Worth running the same query (`Option::where('name_nl','like','%erbruik%')`) before
anyone trusts that field.

## The other direction

Grepped `nox_value` across `app/` and `database/`: `AfficheController` lines 53, 289 and 351 (the
count, the decision to print, the value on the card), the schema dump, the sheet field
(`options.blade.php`) and the labels in `resources/lang/*/vehicle.php`. There is **no** observer,
job, command or migration that copies an option into the column, so this change duplicates nothing.
`VehicleObserver`, `TransportObserver`, `DealerObserver` and `SettingObserver` do not mention NOx.

## Existing rows

There is nothing to backfill: the option never held the value, so there is no second copy to recover
it from. Vehicles fetched before this fix simply have no NOx, their Energy Card will keep failing,
and that stays true until someone supplies the value.

Two ways out, and both are a decision for Shane and Ilse rather than a migration:

1. Type it in from the certificate, per vehicle, as dealers do today.
2. Fetch the VIN again, which now writes the column - but that is a billed AutoConnect lookup, so it
   costs a token per vehicle.

No data migration in this PR, and none proposed: it is the day before the cutover.

How many vehicles it concerns (read-only, safe to run on production):

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS zonder_nox
FROM vehicles
WHERE (nox_value IS NULL OR nox_value <= 0)
  AND fuel_type_id <> 3
  AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND sold = 0;
```

(Fuel type 3 is electric; those get a card without NOx, see R S2-9.3.)

## Checked

- Tests: `tests/Feature/NoxFromLookupTest.php`. A response carrying `NoxEngineTest` puts the number
  in `nox_value` and creates **no** option row for the vehicle; "22 mg/km" and "0,4" are normalised;
  a value with no number ("onbekend") and an absent value leave the column alone; and the Energy Card
  check counts the vehicle as missing NOx before the lookup and as having it after. The fixture
  deliberately creates the four options the mapping needs to run and *not* a NOX option, so the test
  world matches production. Mutation-checked: dropping the column write fails three tests, writing
  the raw unparsed value fails two.
- `php artisan test --filter='OwnStock|Vehicle|Affiche|Vwe|AutoConnect|SmokeTest|Nox|RulesCoverage'`
  green (786 assertions) on a MariaDB loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the
  post-2026-07-28 migrations, the way CI does it.
- Rules: R S1-7.6 now says the value goes to `nox_value`, how it is parsed, and what was wrong
  before; stand moves from `betwist` to `code`. R S2-9.1 (the Energy Card needs NOx) gains the
  electric exception it was missing and moves from `betwist` to `code`, which is what X-72 was about;
  X-72 and X-44 move to the "Opgelost" table with their outcome, and O-10 ("mapping nakijken") goes.
  `92-testdekking.md` and `bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated with `bin/rules-coverage --write` and
  `bin/rules-page`. Note the snapshot on main was already one rule stale (76, not the 75 it claimed);
  regenerating picks that up too.
- **Rebase warning:** another branch, `docs/rules-up-to-date`, is rewriting the same rule documents
  right now. This PR touches only the two rules, the two findings and the one open point it
  resolves, plus the two generated files. If that branch lands first, the generated files here will
  conflict and should simply be regenerated with the two commands above.
params.title: Chassis lookup: NOx goes into nox_value
